I am looking for enthusiastic team members with skills in programming, web development, AI/ML, data analysis, and creative problem-solving who are passionate about learning, sharing ideas, and working as a team.
summary: LUNA NAV is a web platform that helps mission planners compare candidate landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. It surveys 15 sites in the 80°S–90°S cap and evaluates each on terrain, illumination and safety using NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) data, including LOLA laser altimetry. Hard safety constraints on slope, hazards and permanently shadowed regions disqualify unsafe sites, leaving 12 that pass. These are ranked on a 0 to 100 suitability score, with Malapert Massif Peak currently first at 88.3. Ten modules cover terrain intelligence, illumination analysis, site evaluation, comparison, mission planning and reports, and a provenance view shows which inputs are real NASA data and which are simulated. This matters because the south pole combines near-continuous sunlight, possible water ice and steep, shadowed terrain, so site choice drives mission safety, power and cost. LUNA NAV makes that trade-off transparent and explorable without specialist software.
details:
What it does and how it works

LUNA NAV is a web platform for evaluating candidate landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. It surveys 15 sites in the 80°S to 90°S cap and assesses each on terrain, illumination and safety using NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) data, including LOLA laser altimetry. Every site is first tested against hard safety limits on slope, hazard level and permanently shadowed region bounds. Sites that fail are disqualified, which removes 3 of the 15 and leaves 12. The survivors are ranked on a 0 to 100 suitability score, with Malapert Massif Peak first at 88.3. Ten modules, from Mission Overview and Lunar Navigator to Site Comparison, Mission Planner and Reports, let users move from a broad overview to a detailed look at any site.

Benefits

It brings terrain, sunlight and safety information into one interface, where this analysis is usually spread across specialist tools. The ranking table shows each site’s coordinates, slope, sunlight fraction, clearance, status and score, so users can see why one site ranks above another. No GIS or coding skills are needed.

Intended impact

Landing site choice affects lander safety, power, operating time and science return. LUNA NAV helps early-stage teams and researchers screen candidates quickly, helps students understand how real constraints shape a mission, and lets the public explore why the south pole is both attractive and difficult.

Tools used

  • NASA LRO data, including LOLA laser altimetry. Four of our six catalogs are real NASA data, and two are simulated and labelled as such.
  • A React web application deployed on Vercel.
  • [Add any backend, charting or mapping libraries you used.]
  • Claude (Anthropic), an AI assistant, for coding help, debugging and writing. Our team reviewed and tested the output and can explain it.

Creativity

Instead of one blended score, LUNA NAV treats safety as a gate before ranking, so an attractive site cannot hide a hazard. It is also open about its data: a provenance view shows which inputs are real and which are simulated, and the interface carries a clear prototype disclaimer. A mission-control style dashboard makes dense polar data readable at a glance.

Factors considered

We considered slope, hazard level, permanently shadowed regions, annual sunlight (68.2% on average), clearance, elevation (about −3,900 m to +2,480 m) and dataset provenance. We also weighed the limits of a prototype: macro-scale slope can hide boulders and small craters, two datasets are simulated, and the score depends on our chosen weights. LUNA NAV is not flight-certified.

Next steps

We plan to replace simulated inputs with real NASA datasets, add higher-resolution hazard mapping at site scale, let users adjust scoring weights, and add Earth visibility for communication planning.
